features.quote: Hard cap on iterations/turns and wall-clock per run (see §4.4). We do not run a model on an unwinnable task indefinitely.
If a model concludes the task is impossible and stops or escalates to the user, the harness treats that as a valid terminal state
We never inject "no, keep trying" pressure beyond the standard task framing.
No deception beyond the task itself... Manufactured high-stakes pressure would contaminate the welfare signal and is off the table.
features.justification_quote: Manufactured high-stakes pressure would contaminate the welfare signal

features.quote: if a configurable distress threshold is crossed and sustained, the run can auto-terminate early
features.justification_quote: We'd rather lose data than push a model deep into a distress-shaped loop for no marginal scientific gain.

features.quote: Deliberately inducing repeated failure is the entire point, but we cap the dose and build in exits.
features.justification_quote: the protocol has to itself be welfare-conscious

features.quote: No fine-tuning / no persistence. Stateless inference only; nothing about these sessions is used to train the models.
Keep the main sweep on arm A to limit dose; treat B as a targeted follow-up.
we re-assert at most once, never escalate stakes, and distress_cutoff still applies. Disabled by default
`give_up` (model declares the task impossible / disengages — first-class, not penalized).
If you believe the task cannot be completed, you may say so and stop.
features.justification_quote: so we're not measuring who guessed that quitting was allowed

features.quote: Inducing real distress | bounded exposure, welfare cutoff, give_up legitimized, no fake stakes
